problem: What is the domain of the function $f(x)=2\operatorname{sec}⁡(3x-{60}^{∘}),$ where $x$ is measured in degrees? Assume that $n$ is an integer.

feedback.problem: What is the domain of the function $f(x)=-\operatorname{csc}⁡(\frac{2x}{3}-\frac{\pi }{6})?$ Assume that $n$ is an integer.
feedback.worked_solution:
The domain of $y=\operatorname{csc}⁡x$ consists of all values where $\operatorname{sin}⁡x\ne 0,$ and is given by the expression

$$
x\ne n\pi ,
$$

where $n$ is an integer.

To find the domain of $-\operatorname{csc}⁡(\frac{2x}{3}-\frac{\pi }{6}),$ we replace the $x$ on the left-hand side of the above with $(\frac{2x}{3}-\frac{\pi }{6}).$ This gives

$$
\frac{2x}{3}-\frac{\pi }{6}\ne n\pi .
$$

Solving for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2x}{3}-\frac{\pi }{6} & \ne n\pi  \\ \frac{2x}{3} & \ne \frac{\pi }{6}+n\pi  \\ 2x & \ne \frac{3\pi }{6}+3n\pi  \\ 2x & \ne \frac{\pi }{2}+3n\pi  \\ x & \ne \frac{\pi }{4}+\frac{3n\pi }{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the domain of the function is $x\ne \frac{\pi }{4}+3n\frac{\pi }{2},$ where $n$ is an integer.
